The generic finiteGram_right_orbit_complete theorem in D0.Algebra is the shared orbit API and is directly consumed by the concrete IsRoleLorentz specialization; it requires an invertible reference frame but does not require eta to be invertible. The generic finiteGram_dressed_transport_compatible theorem now owns the frame-dressed endpoint Gram identity, and a4dDressedLink_metric_compatible specializes it with the existing IsRoleLorentz hypothesis and target-frame invertibility condition unchanged. The field theorem retains all-site nondegeneracy and refines to the determinant-one subgroup only when the two solder fields have equal determinant orientation at every site. This records proper determinant orientation but leaves time orientation unrestricted; the stronger SO+(1,3) source restriction is still open. The pinned source's endpoint isometry is proved for each link satisfying IsRoleLorentz, with invertibility required only at its target solder frame; the field corollary states the exact Q/K metric relation. For B, the source-convention adapter maps its frame by right multiplication with eta into the existing solder Gram carrier, retains the quadratic remainder, and proves the full finite-matrix Frechet derivative at the flat frame. The shared algebra layer now proves the generic finiteGram derivative at every frame; the pinned flat J2 derivative is its specialization through H ↦ 1+H. That derivative composes with the finite solder readout over arbitrary LocalCoframeField N perturbations and is collected into one Frechet derivative for the whole output field x ↦ solderMetricMatrix N e x, whose value at each site is exactly the existing coframeMetricReadout. Matrix derivatives use the Frobenius norm and full fields use inherited finite Pi norms.
